blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust in the Oil & Gas context — regulation-first design, a fixed delivery rhythm, and outcomes your board can audit.

Upstream and downstream operators run hazardous physics under volatile markets: predictive integrity, energy efficiency, trading precision and OT security decide both margin and license to operate. Every program must respect process-safety culture from day one.

items: Convergence and legacy SCADA create attack paths with physical consequence; 62443 incomplete.
Pipelines, separators and rotating equipment hold failure precursors nobody sees; integrity runs on schedules.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Integrity management, Turnaround scheduling, Trading and scheduling) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Process safety (Seveso/OSHA PSM) among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
62443 zoning with monitoring and access control (attack paths closed)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Energy & Utilities level this capability reads as: restoration-tested backups and manual-fallback procedures (cyber events rehearsed as outages). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
